references.text: The priest dips his finger in the blood and sprinkles it, a parallel to Eleazar's action with the red heifer.
Sprinkling of blood seven times before the tent of meeting as part of the cleansing ritual.
Sprinkling seven times as part of the cleansing process, following the same pattern as with the red heifer.
Sprinkling of blood with the finger seven times, a central element in the Day of Atonement ritual.
The priest sprinkles blood seven times to cleanse and consecrate the altar.
Sprinkling before the Lord's presence as part of the consecration ritual.
The Letter to the Hebrews refers to the blood of the red heifer that is sprinkled to cleanse what is unclean, pointing toward Christ's perfect sacrifice.
Jesus' blood that speaks more strongly than Abel's blood, a fulfillment of the symbolism of blood sprinkling.
